﴿He is Allah﴾: He is the one who alone possesses divinity and is specific to it. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾: this affirms that, like your saying "The qibla is the Ka'ba, there is no qibla but it." ﴿To Him belongs praise in the first and the last﴾: in this world and the Hereafter. This is their saying, ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has removed grief from us﴾ [Fatir: 34] (p-655) ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾ [al-Zumar: 74] ﴿And it will be said: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Zumar: 75]. Praise there is given with pleasure, not with effort. ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾: the judging among His servants. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ by resurrection and raising up. Ya'qub reads it with the tā' pointed with a fatḥa (بِفَتْحِ التاءِ) and the jīm pointed with a kasra (وكَسْرِ الجِيمِ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 71:

﴿Say: "Have you considered?"﴾ With the hamza elided, according to ʿAlī (the reading attributed to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib). ﴿If Allah makes the night perpetual for you﴾ — "perpetual" (sarmadan) is the second object of ja'ala (made). That is, lasting, continuous, from al-sard (sard), which means successive continuation. From it comes their saying concerning the sacred months: "three in succession (sard) and one single (fard)." The mīm is additional, and its measure is faʿmal. ﴿Until the Day of Resurrection. Who is a god other than Allah who would bring you light? Will you not hear?﴾ The meaning is: tell me, who is able to do this?

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 72:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if Allah were to make the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a god other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you may rest? Will you not then see?﴾ He did not say "with a day in which you may engage in livelihood" as He said "with a night in which you may rest," but rather He mentioned the light (ḍiyāʾ), which is the light of the sun, because the benefits connected with it are numerous: engaging in livelihood is not the only one. Darkness does not hold this rank, and therefore He paired ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ with light, while pairing ﴿Will you not then hear?﴾ with night. This is because hearing perceives what sight does not perceive, namely the mention of its benefits and the description of its advantages. And He paired ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ with night because someone else sees, from the benefit of darkness, what you see from stillness and the like.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 73:**

﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ That is: that you may rest by night and seek of Allah's bounty by day, so this is from the figure of *al-laff wa al-nashr* (the rhetorical device of mentioning two things and then assigning each to its counterpart without specifying which goes with which). ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾ to Allah for His blessings. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible that its meaning is: that you may rest in both of them and seek Allah's bounty in both of them, and the meaning would be: He made time for you as night and day, that you may rest in it and seek of His bounty in it. (p-656)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 74:

﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ He repeated the rebuke for taking partners (shuraka') in order to signal that nothing attracts the wrath of Allah more than associating partners with Him, just as nothing brings His good pleasure more than affirming His oneness (tawhid).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 75:

﴿And We shall draw out﴾ and bring forth ﴿from every nation a witness﴾, meaning: their prophet, because the prophets are witnesses over their nations, testifying to what they were upon. ﴿Then We shall say﴾ to the nations, ﴿"Bring your proof"﴾ concerning what you were upon of polytheism and opposition to the messengers. ﴿Then they will know﴾ at that time ﴿that the truth belongs to Allah﴾, that is, monotheism (tawhid), ﴿and what they used to fabricate will have strayed from them﴾ and will have been lost to them, with the absence of a lost thing, concerning the divinity of other than Allah and their intercession.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 76:

﴿Indeed, Qarun﴾ is not declined (lā yanṣarif) because of its foreignness (ʿujma, non-Arabic origin) and its definiteness (taʿrīf). Even if it were of the pattern fāʿūl from qarantu al-shayʾ (I joined the thing), it would be declined. ﴿was of the people of Musa﴾: he was an Israelite, a paternal cousin of Musa. He was Qarun ibn Yasˤhar ibn Qahith ibn Lawi ibn Yaʿqub, and Musa was ibn ʿImran ibn Qahith. He was called "al-Munawwar" (the Illuminated) for the beauty of his appearance. He was the most proficient of the Children of Israel in the Torah, but he became a hypocrite, just as al-Samiri became a hypocrite. ﴿So he oppressed them﴾: from al-baghy, which is injustice (ẓulm). It was said: Pharaoh made him ruler over the Children of Israel, and he wronged them. Or, from al-baghy meaning arrogance: he acted arrogantly towards them through the abundance of his wealth and children. Or, he exceeded them in garments by a span (shibr).

﴿And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys﴾: mā here means alladhī (that which), in the accusative position as the object of ātaynā. Inna with its subject and predicate is the relative clause (ṣila) of alladhī; for this reason inna is kasra-marked. Al-mafātiḥ is the plural of miftaḥ (with kasra), which is that by which something is opened, or of mafταḥ (with fatḥa), which means a storehouse (khizāna). The more correct view is that it means the keys (al-maqālīd).

﴿Would weigh down a band﴾: to weigh down (litunqila) the band. The bāʾ here is for transitivity (lil-taʿdiya); it is said nāʾa bihi al-ḥimlu when the load weighed heavily on him until it inclined him. ʿUṣba (band) means a large group. He had sixty mules carrying the keys to his treasuries, one key for each treasury, and the key would not exceed a finger in size, and they were made of leather.

﴿The people of strength﴾: those of might (al-shidda). ﴿When his people said to him﴾: i.e., the believers. It was also said the speaker was Musa, peace be upon him. (p-657) The position of idh is in the accusative, governed by tanūʾ.

﴿Do not exult﴾: do not be insolent (lā tabṭar) with the abundance of wealth, as in His saying: ﴿And do not exult in what He has given you﴾ [al-Hadid: 23]. Only one who is content with this world and at rest in it exults in the world. As for one whose heart is set on the Hereafter, and who knows that he will leave it soon, he does not exult in it. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾: those insolent with wealth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 77:

﴿And seek, in what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ from wealth and riches, by giving charity to the poor, maintaining the ties of kinship, and spending on the avenues of good. ﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾, which is to take what suffices you and sets your affairs right. It was also said that its meaning is: seek your Hereafter through your worldly life, for that is the believer's portion of it. ﴿And be good﴾ to the servants of Allah ﴿as Allah has been good to you﴾, or: be good by thanking and obeying the Creator of mankind, as He has been good to you with favours. ﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾ by oppression and tyranny. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾.

He said, "I have been given it only on account of knowledge I possess," that is, the wealth, "on the basis of deserving it because of the knowledge that is in me, by which I have been favoured over people," and this is the knowledge of the Torah, or the knowledge of alchemy (al-kimiya'), for he used to take lead and copper and turn them into gold, or the knowledge of the ways of gain through trade and agriculture. And "with me" (ʿindi) is an attribute of "knowledge." Sahl said: "No one looked at himself and prospered. The fortunate one is the one whose sight is turned away from his own actions and words, and the path of seeing the favour of God Most High upon him in all actions and words is opened to him. The wretched one is the one who beautifies in his eyes his own actions, words and states, so he takes pride in them and claims them for himself, and his ill omen destroys him one day, just as Qarun was swallowed up by the earth when he claimed merit for himself."

﴿Did he not know﴾ Qarun ﴿that God had already destroyed before him generations of those who were greater than him in strength﴾. This is an affirmation of his knowledge that God had already destroyed, from the generations before him, those who were stronger and richer than him, because he had read of it in the Torah, as if it were said: "Or did he not know, among the totality of the knowledge he possesses, this, so that he would not be deceived by the abundance of his wealth" (p-658) "and his strength?" Or it is a negation of his knowledge of that, because when he said, "I have been given it on the basis of knowledge with me," it was said: "Does he have knowledge like that which he claims, and sees himself thereby as deserving of every blessing, and yet does not know this beneficial knowledge by which he could protect himself from the fates of those who perished?" ﴿And greater in number﴾ in wealth, or greater in company and multitude. ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾ because God knows them; rather they will enter the Fire without reckoning, or they will confess it without being questioned, or they will be recognised by their marks and so will not be asked, or they will not be asked for the purpose of learning anything from them, rather they will be asked a question of rebuke. Or it means: the guilty of this community will not be asked about the sins of past peoples.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 79:**

﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment.﴾ [It was] in red and yellow [garments]. It is said: he went out on a Saturday, riding a grey-white mule with a crimson (*al-urjuwan*) saddle-cloth, and on it were saddles of gold. With him were four thousand [men] dressed in his fashion. It is also said: he and his horses were covered in red brocade (*al-dibaj*). On his right were three hundred boys, and on his left were three hundred white slave-girls, wearing jewelry and brocade. "In his adornment" is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) referring to the subject of *kharaja* (went out), meaning: adorned.

﴿Those who desired the worldly life said﴾: It is said they were Muslims, and that they only wished for this out of a desire for wealth, as is human custom. It is also said they were disbelievers.

﴿"Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given!"﴾ They said this out of *ghibṭah* (envious admiration). The *ghabit* (one who feels *ghibṭah*) is the one who wishes for the like of his companion's blessing without that blessing being removed from him, as in this verse. The *hasid* (envier) is the one who wishes that his companion's blessing would become his own, to the exclusion of the other. This is like the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾ [al-Nisa: 32].

It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Does *ghibṭah* harm?" He said: "No, except as the *khabat* harms the *idah*."

﴿Indeed, he is the possessor of a great fortune.﴾ *Al-hazz* means *al-jadd* (good fortune), which is luck and prosperity.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 80:

﴿And those who had been given knowledge said﴾ — [that is, knowledge of the reward and punishment, of the passing away of this world and the enduring of the Hereafter] — to those who coveted (ghabitun, "those who envied") Qarun: ﴿Woe to you!﴾ The original sense of "waylaka" (woe to you) is a supplication for destruction; then it came to be used for rebuke, deterrence, and urging one to abandon what does not please [God]. In al-Tibyan fi I'rab al-Qur'an [the grammatical analysis of the Qur'an by al-Ukbari], it is stated that "waylakum" is the object of a verb that has been omitted, meaning: "May God impose upon you woe" (alzamakumu Allahu "waylakum"). ﴿The reward of God is better for one who believes and does righteous deeds; but none receives it except the patient.﴾ That is: "wa-la yulaqqaha" means: this word, namely "the reward of God is better," is not conveyed (yulaqqanu) except to the patient, ﴿except the patient﴾ — in obedience, in abstaining from desires and the adornment of this world, and in being content with what God has apportioned of the little in place of the much.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 81:

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home.﴾ Qarun used to harm Musa, peace be upon him, at all times, while Musa tolerated him because of the kinship between them, until the zakat was revealed. So Musa settled with him: from every thousand dinars he would take one dinar, and from every thousand dirhams one dirham. Qarun calculated it and found it too much, and his soul was stingy with it. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said: "Musa wants to take your wealth." They said: "You are our senior; command us as you wish." He said: "Let us set up a prostitute named so-and-so to accuse him by throwing herself at him, so that the Children of Israel will reject him." They agreed, and he gave her a thousand dinars, or a basin of gold, or her own judgment (in his favour). Then, on a day of festival, Musa stood up and said: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we shall cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we shall flog him; and whoever commits fornication while unmarried, we shall flog him, and if he is married, we shall stone him." Qarun said: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Even if it is me." He said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with so-and-so." So she was brought, and he adjured her by Him who split the sea and sent down the Torah, that she tell the truth. She said: "Qarun gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you with myself." Musa fell down in prostration, weeping, and said: "O Lord, if I am Your messenger, then be angry on my behalf." God revealed to him: "Command the earth as you wish, for it obeys you." So he said: "O Children of Israel, God has sent me to Qarun just as He sent me to Pharaoh. Whoever is with him, let him remain in his place; and whoever is with me, let him withdraw." They all withdrew except two men. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" and it seized them up to the knees. Then he said: "Seize them!" and it seized them up to the waists. Then he said: "Seize them!" and it seized them up to the necks. Qarun and his companions were pleading with Musa and adjuring him by God and by kinship, but Musa did not turn to them because of the intensity of his anger. Then he said: "(p-660) Seize them!" and it closed over them. God Most High said: "They cried to you for help many times, and you did not show them mercy. By My might, if he had asked Me for mercy even once, I would have shown him mercy." Some of the Children of Israel said: "He only destroyed him so that he could inherit his wealth." So he prayed to God, until the earth swallowed up his home and his treasures. ﴿So he had no group to help him﴾ — a company — ﴿against God﴾ — to protect him from the punishment of God — ﴿and he was not among those who could defend themselves﴾ — among those who take vengeance upon Musa, or among those who resist the punishment of God. It is said: "He helped him against his enemy, so he defended himself," meaning: he protected him from it, so he resisted.

And those who had wished for his position yesterday (وَأصْبَحَ وصارَ ﴿الَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوْا مَكانَهُ﴾ مَنزِلَتَهُ مِنَ الدُنْيا ﴿بِالأمْسِ﴾) — "and became" means "and turned into," and "those who wished to be in his place" means in his station in worldly life; "yesterday" (bil-amsi) is an adverbial complement governing "wished." It does not mean the day before your day, but rather a near time, used as a metaphor (isti'arah).

﴿They said, "Woe! It is as if Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it..."﴾ — Regarding "wayka'anna" (ويْكَأنَّ): according to the Basrans, "way" (ويْ) is separate from "ka'anna" (كَأنَّ). Sibawayh said: "way" is a word of alerting to error and of regret, which the one who regrets uses to show his remorse. The meaning is that the people became alert to their error in their wishing and their saying, ﴿Would that we had the like of what Qarun was given﴾ [al-Qasas: 79], and they regretted it, ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up.﴾ That is, by diverting from us what we had wished for yesterday. (لَخَسَفَ بِنا) — with two fathas, read by Hafs, Ya'qub and Sahl, and in it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted. ﴿And woe! It is as if the disbelievers do not prosper﴾ — that is, they regretted, then said, "It is as if the disbelievers do not prosper."

That is the abode of the Hereafter. ﴿Tilka﴾ (That) is used to magnify it and to emphasize its status. The meaning is: that which you have heard mentioned and whose description has reached you. His saying ﴿We shall make it﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of ﴿tilka﴾ (That), and "the abode" (al-dar) is its qualifier (na't, adjective). It is for ﴿those who do not desire exaltation on the earth﴾, meaning arrogance (baghy), according to Ibn Jubayr, or wrongdoing (zulm), according to al-Dahhak, ﴿nor corruption﴾, meaning acting in acts of disobedience, or killing a soul, or calling to the worship of other than God. He did not make the promise conditional on abandoning exaltation and corruption, but on abandoning the desire for them and the inclination of the hearts toward them, as He said: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have wronged﴾ [Hud: 113]. Thus He made the threat conditional on inclining (rukun). It is related from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that a man may be pleased that the strap of his sandal is finer than the strap of his companion's sandal, and so he enters under this (verse's warning). It is related from al-Fudayl that he recited it and then said: "Wishful thinking has departed here." It is related from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he kept repeating it until he passed away. Some said: its true meaning is a warning against following Pharaoh and Qarun, relying on His saying: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself on the earth﴾ [al-Qasas: 4], and ﴿And seek not corruption on the earth﴾ [al-Qasas: 77]. ﴿And the final outcome﴾, the praiseworthy one, is ﴿for the righteous﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 84:

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it.﴾

It has passed in al-Naml (the Surah of the Ants) ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [with] what they used to do﴾. Its meaning: "so they will not be recompensed," but He placed "those who did evil deeds" in the position of the pronoun, because attributing the doing of evil deeds to them repeatedly carries an added sense of disparaging their state and an increase in making evil deeds hateful to the hearts of the listeners. ﴿except what they used to do﴾, that is, except the like of what they used to do. And of His great bounty is that He does not recompense an evil deed except with its like, while He recompenses a good deed with ten times its like, and up to seven hundred times.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 85:

﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an for you﴾ made it obligatory upon you to recite it, convey it, and act upon what is in it. ﴿Will surely bring you back﴾ after death ﴿to a place of return﴾, which place? ("To a place of return") is not for anyone other than you among mankind; therefore He made it indefinite (nakkarahu). Or what is meant by it is Makkah, and what is meant is his return to it on the Day of the Conquest (yawm al-Fath), because it was on that day a place of return of great significance (ma'adan lahu sha'nun wa marji'an lahu i'tidad), due to the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his subjugation of its people, and due to the manifestation of the might of Islam and its people and the humiliation of polytheism (shirk) and its party. The surah is Meccan, but this verse was revealed at al-Juhfah, neither in Makkah nor in Madinah, when he longed for his birthplace (mawlid) (p-662) and the birthplace of his forefathers. And when He promised His Messenger the return to a place of return, He said: ﴿Say﴾ to the polytheists: ﴿My Lord knows best who has brought guidance﴾, meaning: himself, and what reward he has in the place of return. ﴿And who is in manifest error﴾, meaning: the polytheists, and what punishment they deserve in their place of return. "Man" (من) is in a position of accusative (nasb) by an implied verb, i.e., "He knows."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 86:

﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be cast down to you﴾ — it is revealed (yuha) to you — ﴿the Book﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾. This is construed according to the sense (mahmul 'ala al-ma'na): that is, "And the Book was not cast down to you except as a mercy from your Lord," or "except" is in the sense of lakin (but) for istidrak (correction of a preceding statement), that is, "But it was cast down to you, the Book, out of a mercy from your Lord." ﴿So do not be a supporter (zahir) for the disbelievers﴾ — a helper (mu'in) to them in their religion.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 87:

﴿And let them not turn you away from the signs of Allah﴾ The pronoun is in the plural (jam'), meaning: let these people not prevent you from acting upon the signs of Allah, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿after they have been sent down to you﴾, the verses, meaning: after the time of their being sent down. And idh (when/after) is prefixed to time-words, as in your saying ḥīnaʾidh (at that time) and yawmaʾidh (on that day). ﴿And call to your Lord﴾, to His oneness (tawḥīd) and worship, ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 28, verse 88:

﴿And do not invoke with Allah another god.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The address is outwardly to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is the people of his religion. And infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*) does not prevent a prohibition from being addressed. The pause (*waqf*) on "ākhar" (آخَرَ) is obligatory, because if it were connected, then ﴿there is no god but He﴾ would become an attribute of "ilāhan ākhar" (إلَهًا آخَرَ), and there is as much corruption in that as there is.

﴿Everything perishes except His Face.﴾ That is, except Himself. "The face" is used to express the essence. Mujahid said: It means the knowledge of the scholars when it is sought for the sake of Allah's face.

﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾: the decision regarding His creation. ﴿And to Him you will be returned.﴾ With a fatha on the tāʾ and a kasra on the jīm, Yaʿqub (the reciter) reads it so.

And Allah knows best.
